- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After sharp price spikes, model overshoots and fails to correct downward — overestimates continuation of the spike.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after strong upward moves, then underestimates subsequent decline.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Model underestimates volatility in early periods (e.g., after a sharp drop, forecast remains flat or slightly upward).
- In low-volatility periods, model overfits recent trends, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model fails to capture sudden policy or market shocks — often misses abrupt reversals or new regulatory impacts.
- Forecast accuracy improves when model incorporates recent volatility clustering or seasonality adjustments.
- Model overestimates long-term trends (e.g., 30-day horizon) when prices are consolidating or trending sideways.
- Model underestimates downward corrections after upward momentum — fails to recognize “reversal zones” in price behavior.
